speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) what are the circumstances that led to the unintended release of the information on the new mandatory three-year lock-in period for vehicles registered as business-owned private-hire cars, (b) whether an investigation will be conducted into this incident, and (c) whether any steps will be taken to prevent its recurrence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: NCS has taken steps to prevent a recurrence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: MOT will be sharing more details regarding the review of the point-to-point transport sector at the upcoming COS debate and we will address their questions then.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I think the Senior Minister of State for her reply.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the Senior Minister of State able to share what steps NCS has taken to prevent a recurrence?

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And has there been any impact on the execution of this policy due to the implementation being earlier than planned?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As I noted earlier in my reply, this was a deployment error.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The deployment error occurred when the system changes were being deployed to the production environment, that is the actual system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, it resulted in the premature display of this lock-in period message to users who were using the digital service for the relevant vehicle transactions.
